headline: Inferring connectivity distributions from neural dynamics via flow-matching CNFs
label: Inferring Hidden Connectivity Distributions
summary: Recent preprints shift circuit inference toward distributions over hidden connectivity, constrained by ultrastructure and neural recordings.
synthesis: The common thread is constraining models with biological structure to infer quantities that cannot be observed directly. In one preprint, a learned compiler maps molecularly annotated synaptic ultrastructure to simulator-ready, uncertainty-aware neural dynamics. A second preprint uses a maximum-entropy, flow-matching continuous normalizing flow to infer distributions over connectivity in low-rank RNNs from neural recordings. A published Cell Reports study builds biology-constrained ANNs with E/I cell types and dendritic compartments, trained via dendritic target propagation on image classification. What is new in the connectivity preprint is explicit inference of a distribution over connectivity rather than a single estimate. The evidence is heterogeneous: only the flow-based study addresses connectivity inference directly, while the other two bear on it indirectly through structure-to-dynamics mapping and biologically constrained architecture.
